prompt: An ML problem is defined by which three components?
explanation: Only when you can say what goes in, what comes out and what the learning process minimises is a business wish an ML problem.

prompt: A team raises accuracy from 94.0% to 94.2% but no business metric moves. The best conclusion is...
options: accuracy must be raised further before measuring anything else
the ML metric is not yet shown to matter; connect it to a business metric, possibly with an A/B test
business metrics are irrelevant to ML teams
explanation: Companies care about business metrics; ML metrics are proxies whose link must be established.

prompt: Which statement about ML reliability is specific to ML systems?
options: The system can return predictions without any error while the predictions are wrong
Deployments can use the wrong file
explanation: Silent failure is the ML twist: no exception, no 404, just bad predictions.

prompt: A server processes a batch of 50 queries in 20 ms. What is its throughput in queries per second?
Latencies (ms): 100, 102, 100, 100, 99, 104, 110, 90, 3000, 95. Which summary best reveals the problem?
explanation: The mean is misleading and the median hides the outlier; a high percentile exposes the tail.

prompt: Why is it often better to train one model per objective and blend their scores than to train one model on $\alpha L_1+\beta L_2$?
options: Changing the trade-off needs no retraining and models can be maintained on their own schedules
explanation: The dial $\alpha,\beta$ moves to ranking time; spam filters and quality models change at different speeds.

prompt: An article may have several topics and the model outputs [0.45, 0.2, 0.02, 0.33]. What extra decision does the multilabel setting force?
options: How many labels (or what threshold) to extract from the probabilities
Whether to use softmax or sigmoid at test time only
explanation: In multiclass you take the argmax; in multilabel the number of classes per example varies, so you need a rule.

prompt: Batching raises throughput but can also raise latency. Why?
options: Latency and throughput are the same quantity
Requests must wait for the batch to fill and a larger batch takes longer to run
explanation: Per-request wait plus a longer run time per batch increase latency while the number of requests per second grows.
